assertions.name: A1_beta_decoding_is_exact
assertions.source: T^-1 = T-h verified; chains reproduced, maxdiff 0e+00 and 0e+00

assertions.name: A3_beta0_beta1_symmetric_not_sum_only
assertions.source: swap-invariant to 1e-11; equal sums differ, as the commuting product predicts

assertions.name: A4_beta2_dominates
assertions.source: b_2 uniquely positive and largest at both; ratio 8.1x (proton), 1.9x (neutron)

assertions.name: A5_third_route_agrees
assertions.source: margin roots match dual-support bisection to 1e-07, 4e-10

assertions.name: A6_q0_inside_reachable_range
assertions.source: box transitions span [0.0465, 0.6436]; 15/195 below h(q_0); actual chains both above

description: Measures what sets the two dual-vertex transition points that the binding window is the gap between. Writing sigma_g(beta) = sigma_g - beta*h (beta = 0 forward, 1/2 unoriented average, 1 inverse, since T^-1 = T - h in this convention), both nucleon chains are a shared prefix (sigma_0 sigma_1^-1)^3, a three-letter middle sigma_0(b0) sigma_0(b1) sigma_1(b2), and a shared suffix sigma_0^2, with proton b = (0, 1/2, 1/2) and neutron b = (1/2, 1/2, 1) reproducing v_p and v_n to maxdiff exactly 0.0. The whole flavour split is b += (1/2, 0, 1/2). The sigma_1 letter dominates the transition (d h*/d b_2 = +0.424 at the proton, 8x the other two); b_0 and b_1 enter symmetrically because they multiply the same generator, though not through their sum alone. Margin-root bisection reproduces the transitions 0.477184636796 and 0.569840290998, a third independent route after the primal gap window and the dual support. Over the physical box beta in [0,1]^3 the transition spans about 0.046 to 0.649, so h(q_0) = 0.209060299 is INSIDE the reachable range with 15 of 195 box points below it: a straddling pair is not structurally forbidden, and the corpus's specific assignment is what puts both nucleons above.
caveats: NO BETA VALUES ARE PROPOSED, and none should be read out of this. The parametrisation is a re-description that reproduces the existing chains exactly; the box sweep measures what the transition WOULD be at other crossing-branch assignments, in order to establish whether h(q_0) is reachable at all. Which branches the nucleons actually carry is a physical question the chains already answer, and choosing betas to place a transition at q_0 would be exactly the census-fitting this probe series documents elsewhere.

CORRECTION against my own first pass, which located transitions with a single-root bisection over h in [0.02, 3]. That returns garbage where the margin has zero or two roots — it reported h* = 2.0009 for a chain with no root in range at all. Every transition here scans for sign changes on a geometric grid first and bisects only inside a bracketed one. The proton and neutron each have a single crossing, so their values were never affected.

The box sweep is a 6x6x6 grid, so 'spans 0.046 to 0.649' and '15 of 195 below' are grid statistics, not certified extrema of the continuous family. They are sufficient for the claim actually made — that h(q_0) lies strictly between attainable transitions — since specific grid points fall on either side of it.
